The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is working alongside government agencies and private organizations to assist communities heavily affected by Typhoon Tino (Kalmaegi) and Super Typhoon Uwan (Fung-wong), which struck the Philippines only days apart in early November 2025.
 
The Church provided food, clean drinking water, utility services, and temporary shelters, among other basic and emergency needs, to nearly 50,000 individuals in the most affected regions.
 
The Church also opened the doors of more than 240 meetinghouses to members and neighbors of other faiths seeking refuge from the storms or who had been displaced by major flooding. Latter-day Saints across the country contributed warm meals, clothing, bedding, and other essential items to support their communities.
 
Learn more on Church Newsroom. 

https://t.co/42NodMGuOk

LEE JONG SUK FANMEETING IN MANILA CANCELED DUE TO RALLY

READ: Lee Jong Suk's Nov. 30 fan meeting at the Araneta Coliseum has been canceled due to the large-scale rally set on the same date, Korean entertainment agency Ace Factory announces.

"With the scheduled rally on the same date, this decision was made after careful consideration for the safety of the fans, the artist, and all related teams," Ace Factory says in a statement on Monday, Nov. 17.

It assures tickets will be refunded.

Several groups are set to hold another "Trillion Peso March" rally on Nov. 30 to protest the corruption in the government's flood control projects. | https://t.co/AuNWhQqswP intern PJ De Vera

📸 Ace Factory/Instagram

Iglesia Ni Cristo Statement on the Conclusion of the "Rally for Transparency and a Better Democracy"

In a statement released on November 13, 2025, the Iglesia Ni Cristo said that it would mount a three-day rally to highlight the public clamor for a proper and transparent investigation regarding the anomalous flood control projects in the Philippines (Ang Iglesia Ni Cristo ay... - INC News and Updates | Facebook)

Taking into consideration the speed and extent of media coverage, both local and international, that the rally generated, it did not need three days to achieve the goal of sending the message that we are calling for justice, accountability, transparency, and peace.

We thank our friends from the media, both local and international, who covered the event and spread the message of the rally.
We also express our sincere appreciation and gratitude to all our brethren who came to the "Rally for Transparency and a Better Democracy" at the Quirino Grandstand in Manila which started on Sunday, November 16, 2025.

On the second day of the rally, on Monday, November 17, more of our brethren coming from the provinces arrived at the rally venue. This is in answer to the call of the Church Administration to lend our voices to the growing public clamor for government to decisively address the massive corruption that has already affected the country's economy and international standing.

This is also among the fundamental rights granted to citizens of the country - - the right to free speech and peaceful assembly.

We thank all those who made sure that the rally was peaceful, orderly, and disciplined, including those from the Philippine National Police, the national government, and the Manila City government. 

We sincerely appreciate their sacrifices.
From the very start, we have stressed that we are against moves that are against the Constitution.

We started peacefully and we ended peacefully.

For this, we thank the Lord God and we return all glory to Him.

#NET25NewsandInformation
